severity_steps: 1. Phishing with a click is handled as credential compromise (03 rule note).
2. Assets reached by a confirmed login or session: SRV-VPN01 (Medium), SRV-FS01 (High), SRV-DB01 (High).
3. Credential compromise (account used by an attacker), High column (SRV-FS01, A-1005): P2.
4. Data exfiltration (large transfer, confirmed or suspected), High column (SRV-FS01, A-1005): P1.
5. Incident takes the highest part: P1 (01 rule 4.2).

6. SRV-DC01 (Critical) is not counted: only Kerberos traffic to it and no logon on it by amalik (rules.yaml severity.reach, ARCHITECTURE section 11). If it were counted, credential compromise would be P1, data exfiltration would be P1. Incident stays P1.

actions.text: Find every recipient of the message in the email gateway log.
Remove or quarantine the message from all mailboxes.
Block the sender domain and the link domain at the email gateway and the perimeter firewall.
For each recipient, check the firewall logs for a connection to the link address, to find who clicked.
If a click is found, open RB-CRED-02 for that user.
Send a warning notice to all recipients.
Record all findings in the incident ticket.
Call the real user on the phone number in the user directory and ask if the login was theirs.
Disable the account in the directory and end all active VPN and remote sessions of that account.
Block the attacker source IP at the perimeter firewall.
Reset the password only after step 2, through the helpdesk with identity checks. Require new MFA enrollment.
Review all logins by the account in the last 24 hours and list every system it reached.
If phishing was the source, disconnect the user's laptop from the network.
For every system reached, check for further activity. If a large data transfer is seen, open RB-EXFIL-04.
Keep all logs unchanged as evidence.
Find sessions with an unusually large transfer from the source system in the firewall logs. Note the bytes, the times and the destination.
Block the destination address of the transfer.
Keep the evidence: copy the relevant logs. Do not reboot the source server.
Ask the system owner what data the system holds.
Check if file-level audit logs exist. If they do not, record that it is unknown which files were read.
Inform Legal and Compliance if the system holds finance, HR or customer data.
